Zephyr is a performance-first Shopify theme built on a Tailwind CSS pipeline. It pairs a lightweight, fast-loading storefront with a deeply configurable block-based architecture so merchants can compose pages without touching code.

Performance by default — every image uses a responsive <picture> with precisely calculated srcset ladders; below-the-fold sections lazy-render; layout thrash is eliminated via post-paint measurement. Tailwind-driven styling — utilities and atomic classes are generated by Tailwind; component CSS stays lean. 32-shape vocabulary — a unified rounded-* shape system (squircle, arch, blob, petal, drop, diamond…) drives cards, buttons, media and avatars from a single --shape-radius variable. Block architecture — sections are composed of reusable blocks; the same block (e.g. product card, image, FAQ) is reused across home, collection, product and page templates. Refined interactions — slideshows use arrow navigation (no dots); filters, mega-menu and slide-grids are keyboard-accessible.

Getting started — install, customize, support. Theme settings — global colors, typography, cart, swatches and more. Sections — every section and its settings. Blocks — every reusable block. Templates — what each page template includes. Advanced guides — performance architecture. 💡 All configuration happens in Shopify Admin → Online Store → Themes → Customize.

Zephyr is engineered to score well on Lighthouse out of the box. Key techniques: Responsive <picture> everywhere — every image renders a <picture> with a srcset ladder calculated from the actual display width (per breakpoint, per column count), so browsers never download oversized files. Lazy rendering — below-the-fold sections use content-visibility: auto; heavy resources (3D models, video) defer loading until they enter the viewport. No layout thrash — measurement of slide-grid dimensions is moved to a post-paint callback so it never forces a synchronous reflow during initial render. Tailwind pipeline — utilities are tree-shaken into a single lib.css; only used classes ship. Accessibility-aware media — decorative images are marked aria-hidden; interactive elements keep visible focus states.

Upload images at the recommended dimensions; let Zephyr generate the responsive variants. Keep the number of third-party apps minimal — each app script adds to Total Blocking Time. Prefer the theme's built-in filters, mega-menu and reviews over additional apps where possible.

Welcome to the Zephyr theme documentation.
From your Shopify Admin, go to Online Store → Themes. Upload the Zephyr theme zip, or connect it via the Shopify GitHub integration / CLI. Click Customize to open the theme editor.

Zephyr is fully configured through the theme editor — no code required: Theme settings (global): colors, typography, cart behavior, swatches, social links, translations. Sections: add, reorder and configure page sections. Blocks: fine-tune the content inside each section (text, images, product cards, FAQs, etc.).
See Contacting support for response times and how to reach us.

Zephyr follows Shopify's standard section + block model. A section is a full-width building block of a page (e.g. Slideshow, Featured collection, Image with text). A block is a smaller, reusable piece placed inside a section (e.g. a heading, an image, a product card, an FAQ item). Because Zephyr ships a large shared block library, the same block (product card, image, FAQ) behaves consistently everywhere it appears. Edit a block's settings in the theme editor to change only that instance.

Use the Enable spacing toggle on blocks/sections to add consistent vertical padding. Most media supports the unified shape vocabulary — pick a rounded-* value to round cards, buttons and images together.

Global configuration applied to every page via Shopify Admin → Online Store → Themes → Customize → Theme settings. The following groups are available: Base / Layout Typography Colors Assets Swatches Filters Cart Social media Translation Advanced
